DocForge HTML Reference Fixture

This HTML file serves as a reference fixture for the DocForge test suite. It exercises heading detection, paragraph extraction, table parsing, and list handling within the S1 parse stage.

1. Introduction

Hybrid retrieval systems combine dense vector search with sparse keyword matching. The resulting ranked lists are fused using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to produce a single relevance-ordered result set.

2. Pipeline Stages

The DocForge ingestion pipeline consists of the following stages:

  • S0 — Ingest: convert input to PDF via Gotenberg.
  • S1 — Parse: extract IR using Docling or fallback parsers.
  • S2 — Enrich: route figures/tables to OCR and VLM providers.
  • S4 — Chunk: split IR into retrieval units.
  • S5 — Contextualise: prepend title and breadcrumb to embed text.
  • S6 — Embed & Index: generate vectors and upsert into Qdrant.

3. Configuration Parameters

Parameter Default Description
CHUNK_MAX_TOKENS 512 Maximum tokens per text chunk.
CHUNK_OVERLAP_BLOCKS 0 Number of blocks to prepend from the prior chunk.
TEI_BATCH_SIZE 64 Texts per TEI HTTP request.
ENRICH_MAX_BUDGET_USD 0.0 Maximum API spend per pipeline run (0 = unlimited).

4. Retrieval

Dense retrieval uses cosine similarity over 1024-dimensional BGE-M3 embeddings. Sparse retrieval uses SPLADE-style token weights from the same BGE-M3 model. Both vectors are generated in a single HTTP round-trip to the TEI server.

Search results include: chunk text, document filename, page numbers, chunking strategy, token count, and (in debug mode) per-vector ranks explaining the contribution of dense versus sparse retrieval.
